title: Enabling Collaborative Test-Time Adaptation in Dynamic Environment via Federated Learning

problem.claim: Deep learning models degrade when test data diverges from training data, motivating adaptation to unlabeled test data streams.

gap.claim: Independent test-time adaptation across multiple devices does not leverage information from other devices, while changing client distributions make collaborative adaptation difficult.

contributions.claim: Introduces federated learning into test-time adaptation to enable on-the-fly collaboration among devices through local adaptation, server aggregation, and model redistribution.
Proposes server-side Temporal-Spatial Aggregation, using attention to capture intra-client temporal correlations and inter-client spatial correlations.
Proposes heterogeneity-aware augmentation and self-supervised optimization for improved robustness, with TSA designed as a plug-in for distributed test-time adaptation methods.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on multiple datasets are reported to show that TSA outperforms existing methods and remains robust across various heterogeneity levels.

narrative_sequence.summary: Test-time distribution shift can degrade deep learning performance, and TTA adapts models using unlabeled test streams.
Multi-device deployment creates an opportunity for collaboration, but independent TTA cannot use other devices' data and client distributions change dynamically.
Federated learning coordinates local TTA through client updates, server aggregation, and redistribution of the aggregated model.
TSA models temporal correlations within clients and spatial correlations across clients, supplemented by heterogeneity-aware augmentation and self-supervised optimization.
The authors report improved performance over existing methods and robustness across heterogeneity levels, and provide code.

source_observation.claim: Client test distributions may change over time in different ways, and TSA uses temporal-spatial attention to model this heterogeneity.

interpretation.claim: Adaptation aggregation should account for both within-client temporal change and across-client distribution differences.

application.claim: Use time-aware and cross-client aggregation mechanisms for distributed online adaptation under heterogeneous streams.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify which heterogeneity patterns or deployment conditions the method cannot handle.

unknowns: Specific datasets, baselines, metrics, and numerical results are not provided.
The underlying TTA methods, TSA architecture, augmentation procedure, and self-supervised objective are unspecified.
Communication, privacy, computational, and convergence characteristics are not reported.
The limits of robustness across heterogeneity levels are not described.
